content.summary: The integrated proof has a sound order of dependencies. Profile A obtains a nonempty two-outsider class before choosing a row, preserves one synchronized pair of designs throughout the completion and orientation arguments, and obtains its contradiction without assuming the desired exclusion. The final implication uses the inherited bound 81 and both literal exclusions, keeping I(27) explicit.

checks.scope: Profile A argument transitions and absence of circularity
checks.method: Compared Sections 4.1-4.3 with ResidualProfileA.final_count_window in ProfileACounts.lean and the synchronized DesignPair construction, minimum_projections, pair_one_side and same_side_completion in ProfileASplit.lean.
checks.observation: The census relation n2=n0+15 already gives n2 positive, so choosing a two-outsider row to obtain n0 at least nine is not circular. Each six-point union is a true transversal before minimum-transversal structure is invoked. The same left/right design decomposition is fixed for all rows, and swapping exchanges the complete structure, so the one-orientation argument does not silently compare incompatible coordinate choices. Membership in the support union is proved for the needed keys and completions before their projections are counted.

checks.scope: End-to-end terminal implication and literal statement
checks.method: Followed the final theorem through FinalEighty.lean, ProfileAClosed.lean, TwoHighEighty.lean and the inherited unrestricted_eighty_of_three_open_inputs; compared its expanded hypotheses with Sections 1, 2 and 7.
checks.observation: Under I(27), the inherited upper bound first limits any proposed counterexample to 81 members. The boundary classification then yields an actual A or B family; the new exclusions contradict both possibilities, yielding at most 80. The expanded root quantifies over finite distinct four-sets and forbids three distinct petals with any core, including empty. I(27) remains a universally quantified antecedent, and the external theorem enters only the ordinary numerical corollary.
